item.title: Ba Provincial U19 basketball team overcomes funding challenges to compete at national championship
item.description: After raising funds with the help of their parents and supporters to make the trip to Suva, the Ba Provincial Freebird Institute Under-19 boys basketball team is determined to make its mark at the 2026 Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball Championship. Team captain Junior Savenaca Thomas Ratu says preparations have gone well despite the team facing several challenges along the way.
item.content:encoded:
After raising funds with the help of their parents and supporters to make the trip to Suva, the Ba Provincial Freebird Institute Under-19 boys basketball team is determined to make its mark at the 2026 Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball Championship.

Team captain Junior Savenaca Thomas Ratu says preparations have gone well despite the team facing several challenges along the way.

Ratu says the school is well known for rugby, and with much of its sporting funding going towards rugby, the basketball team had to find other ways to raise money to compete at the championship.

He says the players organised fundraising activities, while parents also stepped in to help cover their expenses.

The Year 13 student says the team is grateful to the parents, families and supporters who helped make their participation possible.

Ratu says their goal is not only to win, but also to make a name for Ba Provincial Freebird Institute and represent the wider Ba community with pride.

He says the team is confident heading into the competition and is ready to face the challenges from other schools.

Ratu says International Secondary School is one of the teams they expect to provide a tough challenge when they meet tomorrow.

He has thanked the team's families, friends and supporters for helping with fundraising, supporting the players and keeping them in their prayers.

Ba Provincial Freebird Institute will take on Jai Narayan College at Yat Sen Secondary School at 8.40 tonight.

item.content:encoded:
70 secondary school from across Fiji will battle over three days in the 2026 Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball Championship as Basketball Fiji looks to identify young talent and continue growing the sport in the country.

The teams are competing in the Under-15, Under-17 and Under-19 grades, with the championship officially opened at Yat Sen Secondary School and the finals to be held at the Vodafone Arena.

Basketball Fiji President Oliver Whippy says the competition has provided a strong platform for young players over the years, with some impressive talent emerging from the tournament.

Whippy says they hope competitions like this will continue to help basketball grow and develop in Fiji, while giving students an opportunity to showcase their skills.

She is encouraging parents, families and school communities to come out and support the players, saying spectators can expect an exciting three days of basketball and an opportunity to see some of Fiji's promising young talent in action.

While opening the championship, Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro says the strong participation reflects the growing interest in basketball and highlights the important role school sports play in developing young people.

Radrodro says sport is an important part of education as it teaches students discipline, teamwork, cooperation, respect and how to make decisions under pressure.

He says basketball also teaches students how to recover from mistakes, accept the decisions of officials and continue working together as a team.

Radrodro highlighted Fiji's recent basketball achievements, including the men's gold medal and women's bronze medal at the 2023 Pacific Games.

He says Fiji's men's and women's teams later won gold at the Mini Pacific FIBA 3x3 Games and qualified for the FIBA 3x3 World Cup in 2025.

Radrodro says these achievements should inspire students and show them what can be achieved through dedication, hard work and continued development.

He has also acknowledged principals, teachers, coaches, parents, families, referees, officials, facilitators and volunteers for their role in supporting young players and developing the sport.

Vodafone Fiji is the major sponsor of the championship, while support has also been provided by Basketball Fiji, FIBA Oceania, the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and programmes supported by the New Zealand and Australian High Commissions.

This includes the Basketball for Good Facilitators Workshop, which focuses on using basketball for community and social development.

With the championship being held during the school holidays, Radrodro has encouraged students to enjoy their break responsibly, remain active and make choices that keep them safe.

He has urged players to compete with courage, discipline and respect, accept both wins and losses and learn from every game.

Radrodro says while the scoreboard records the result, the character players show and the way they conduct themselves will be remembered long after the competition.

item.title: Rewa targets historic 10th BOG title after last year’s heartbreak
item.description: Stratum/PPCL Rewa will be looking to turn last year's disappointment into motivation when they begin their 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants campaign in Ba next week. The Delta Tigers, who have won the Battle of the Giants nine times, will be aiming to reach double figures by securing their 10th title.
item.content:encoded:
Stratum/PPCL Rewa will be looking to turn last year's disappointment into motivation when they begin their 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants campaign in Ba next week.

The Delta Tigers, who have won the Battle of the Giants nine times, will be aiming to reach double figures by securing their 10th title.

Rewa last lifted the BOG trophy in 2020 and finished runners-up to Labasa in last year's tournament.

Fiji Football Association says they now face a challenging Pool B alongside Ba, Lautoka and Nadi .

Rewa will begin their campaign against Lautoka next week Friday at 5pm and will then face hosts Ba on Saturday at 5.30pm, before completing their pool matches against Nadi on Sunday at 1.30pm.

With three tough matches in three days, Rewa will need a strong start if they are to secure a place in the semi-finals.

Meanwhile, BOG will kick start from next Friday at Four R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.

item.title: Springboks must find answers to All Blacks’ breakdown pressure
item.description: Springboks halfback Cobus Reinach says South Africa must find a way to deal with New Zealand’s pressure at the breakdown and produce quicker ball if they are to win the second Test in Cape Town. The All Blacks beat the Springboks 33-16 in the opening Test in Johannesburg, moving to the top of the World Rugby rankings.
item.content:encoded:
Springboks halfback Cobus Reinach says South Africa must find a way to deal with New Zealand’s pressure at the breakdown and produce quicker ball if they are to win the second Test in Cape Town.

The All Blacks beat the Springboks 33-16 in the opening Test in Johannesburg, moving to the top of the World Rugby rankings.

South Africa had several chances inside the New Zealand 22 but managed only one try as handling errors and strong defence from the All Blacks kept the hosts under pressure.

The Springboks were also reduced to 13 men late in the match after Reinach and another player were sent to the sin-bin.

Reinach says New Zealand’s pressure forced South Africa into mistakes.

He says the Springboks must learn from the defeat and find better ways to handle the All Blacks’ defence.

All Blacks will face South Africa this Sunday at 3am in Cape Town.
